title: Deployment Cascade Controller with Compatibility Shims
creator: Sana Patel
description:
Summary:
Build a Deployment Cascade Controller (DCC) — an intelligent routing proxy and orchestration layer that coordinates canary rollouts, A/B tests, shadow traffic, and automated rollback across heterogeneous region and capacity tiers. The DCC will centralize compatibility checks, preflight probes, and tier-aware failover logic so model variant deployments can be safely exercised without manual intervention.

Why this work:
Current rollout primitives are fragmented: per-service routing rules, ad-hoc runbooks for region failover, and limited semantic compatibility signals. This leads to slow canaries, manual rollbacks, and customer-facing regressions when KV cache formats or tokenization differences create silent fidelity issues. DCC aims to codify safety gates and graceful fallbacks to reduce rollout MTTR and avoid cross-tenant impact while preserving fast iteration for model teams.

Scope / high-level behavior:
- Accepts a Deployment Plan (model variants, region priorities, capacity tiers, rollout phases) and exposes a single routing endpoint used by the frontend/router.
- Orchestrates traffic splits for canary/A-B (percentages + shadow lanes) and enforces compatibility shims for KV cache and tokenizer differences before allowing live traffic.
- Runs automated preflight probes (synthetic prompts, perf microbenchmarks, and divergence checks) and uses an SLO/quality gate to advance phases.
- Implements tiered fallback: within-region variant fallback -> cross-region spillover -> capacity-tier degrade (e.g., move from low-latency to high-throughput model variant) -> safe-throttle/queue when no variant is compatible.
- Auto-rollback triggers based on multi-signal rules (increased user error rates, latency p99 breach, semantic drift on eval prompts, embedding/LLR drop) with hysteresis to avoid flip-flop.
- Observability hooks for per-phase metrics, per-tenant rollouts, and traceable decision reasons for any fallback or rollback.

Compatibility shim concept:
- Lightweight adaptation layer that detects common incompatibilities (KV cache layout, kv cache segment boundary, tokenizer vocab differences, param shape mismatches) and either: 1) rejects a variant for live traffic, 2) applies a non-destructive shim (e.g., translate kv keys, map tokenizer ids via mapping table), or 3) warms a compatibility cache with conversion artifacts. Shims are registered per model family and can be toggled per-customer during rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: DCC exposes a deployment API that takes a plan and returns a rollout run_id
Automated preflight probes run and produce a pass/fail summary before non-zero live allocation
Traffic splits for canary/A-B + shadowing are applied atomically and observable in Console
Fallback path executes in less than configured SLA (e.g., 15s) when a variant fails health checks
Auto-rollback triggers based on at least 3 independent signals and records rollback reason in audit logs
Compatibility shims can be registered and tested via unit harness without restarting runtime nodes
End-to-end demo: cross-region canary that falls back to primary region under simulated capacity loss
Integration tests for KV cache conversion shim with warm cache hit rate > 90% after warmup
tasks: Design API schema for Deployment Plan + run_id lifecycle
Prototype shim registry and simple tokenizer id-mapping shim
Implement routing proxy hook into existing request router (feature-flagged)
Build preflight probe runner and synthetic prompt library
Wire Console dashboards for phase/variant metrics and decision traces
Create end-to-end chaos test for cross-region failover (local harness)
Write integration tests covering shard-level KV cache compatibility scenarios
Prepare runbook and SDK helpers for model teams to author shims
